title: Rigatoni with turkey and turnip ragù

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain whole food or a basic like tinned tomatoes, tomato purée, dried pasta and Parmesan, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Turkey mince, turnips, rigatoni and Parmesan are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a pasta pan and a grater, and the techniques are browning, simmering and boiling pasta.

works.reason: 500g turkey, three turnips, a tin of tomatoes with 200ml water and 350g pasta make a well-balanced sauce for four, and small turnip cubes will be tender after 20 minutes' simmering.

honest_times.reason: Chopping the onion, garlic and turnips fits around 16 minutes of browning and softening within the 25 prep minutes, and the 20-minute simmer matches the cook time, with the pasta easily boiled alongside.

honest_ingredients.reason: Rigatoni is a fair name for dried pasta, every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm pasta sauce suits a mid-October lunch, and the turnips are a main component of the sauce named in the title rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, and ragù is a familiar word on UK menus and jars.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling, family-friendly pasta with lean protein, vegetables and tomatoes.
